content: IFT140, also known as Intraflagellar Transport 140 homolog, is a protein in humans that is encoded by the IFT140 gene. Mutations in the IFT140 gene have been linked to cases of skeletal ciliopathy, a group of disorders characterized by defects in the structure or function of cilia, which are microscopic, hair-like structures on the surface of cells. To study the function of IFT140, model organisms have been utilized. A conditional knockout mouse line, named Ift140<sup>tm1a(KOMP)Wtsi</sup>, was developed at the Wellcome Trust Sanger Institute. Both male and female mice from this line underwent a standardized phenotypic screening process to assess the effects of the gene deletion.
